title: Abba bar Huna (or bar Rav Chuna)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman says that Rabbah bar Rav Huna is called this in the Jerusalem Talmud: Terumot 1:4; the beginning of Shabbat chapter 11; Eruvin 1:1, with the additional printed locator ה., then 3:3 and 6:7; Bava Kamma 4:5; Shevuot 2:3. See his entry.

notes.text: The extra Eruvin locator ה. may be a folio reference, but its relation to the surrounding chapter/halakhah labels remains unresolved. Abba/Rabbah is an identification made by the notice, not a canonical name change.

Supplied כ תרומות and the extra Eruvin ה. are retained as textual questions; no folio5 or invented amud is supplied. The body gives full Rabbah bar Rav Huna while the heading has Abba bar Huna or bar Rav Chuna; their connection is Hyman’s designation, not an admitted canonical rename. The whole citation sequence and his-entry pointer remain intact. No new scan, genealogy or chapter-wide primary inspection was performed.

Printed Hyman (vol. I, pp. 42–43) has contiguous כתרומות and retains the extra ה. after Eruvin 1:1. In the consulted Vilna page markers, the Abba bar Huna statement falls on 5b, before 6a. This still leaves Hyman’s extra locator unexplained. The consulted passages have Abba bar Rav Huna in Terumot 1:4 and Bava Kamma 4:4, Ba bar Chuna reporting Rav in Shabbat 11:1, Abba bar Rav Chuna in Eruvin 3:3, Abba bar Chuna reporting Yochanan in Eruvin 6:7, and Abba bar Huna in Shevuot 2:3. Hyman gives Bava Kamma 4:5. The variant names are reported as they stand in each witness.
